cohort: 592 women who delivered at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania from October 15, 2013 through December 15, 2013
finding: While estimated blood loss was significantly lower for vaginal delivery compared to cesarean delivery, the actual blood loss, as measured by hemoglobin drop, was more similar between the two modes of delivery, supporting the use of a single definition of PPH regardless of mode of delivery.
mod_finding: The association between estimated blood loss and observed hemoglobin drop differed in accuracy by mode of delivery, suggesting that blood loss estimation may be less accurate for vaginal deliveries.
